grants.name: Oregon Capacity Building & Community Grant Program

grants.deadline_note: Applications accepted through June 26, 2026. Notifications by Sept 11, 2026. Grant period Oct 1, 2026 – Dec 1, 2027.
grants.fit: High – directly aimed at Oregon land trusts for capacity building and community engagement.
grants.eligibility: Oregon land trusts. 2025 recipients are still eligible to reapply.
grants.use: Capacity building, community engagement, strategic planning. NOT general operating support or land-acquisition capital.

Awards typically range $15K–$35K, with partnership-focused projects able to request extended grant periods. As a CLT, Proud Ground is squarely within the eligible applicant pool. Note this is the closest deadline—confirm exact submission cutoff time on the portal.

grants.name: Housing Program — General Operating & Project Support
grants.funder: Meyer Memorial Trust
grants.deadline_note: Rolling/invitation and cyclical funding windows. Confirm current open call on Meyer's site; timing varies year to year.
grants.fit: Very High – Meyer explicitly funds affordable housing production, preservation, policy, and prioritizes BIPOC-led / BIPOC-serving organizations.
grants.eligibility: Oregon nonprofits; prioritizes organizations led by or serving communities most impacted by systemic inequity.
grants.use: Affordable housing production, preservation, policy advocacy. Meyer notably offers multi-year GENERAL OPERATING support—rare and high-value.
needed: Confirm current funding window on Meyer site
grants.summary: Meyer Memorial Trust is one of the best strategic fits for Proud Ground: it funds Oregon's housing crisis through production, preservation, and policy, and prioritizes BIPOC-led and BIPOC-serving organizations. Critically, Meyer offers multi-year general operating support rather than narrow project grants—extremely valuable for sustainability. Verify the exact current application window, which shifts annually.

grants.name: Housing Development Grant Program (HDGP / Trust Fund)
grants.funder: Oregon Housing and Community Services (OHCS)
grants.deadline_note: Awarded via competitive Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) rounds announced periodically. Monitor OHCS for the next NOFA.
grants.fit: Medium – HDGP centers on multifamily/rental, but OHCS administers multiple homeownership and development resources worth tracking.
grants.eligibility: Nonprofit housing developers, local housing authorities, Tribal housing entities, and for/nonprofit sponsors depending on program.
grants.use: Construct new housing, acquire/rehabilitate structures, or operate housing for low-income households.
grants.summary: OHCS is the state's central affordable-housing funder, deploying capital through competitive NOFA rounds and tax-credit allocations. While HDGP itself leans toward multifamily rental, OHCS administers a broad set of homeownership and development resources (including LAP Homeownership funds that reopened in 2026). Set up monitoring of OHCS NOFA announcements so you catch the next relevant round.

grants.name: Strategic Projects: Program & Staff / Equipment & Technology Grants
grants.funder: M.J. Murdock Charitable Trust
grants.amount: Capacity-building grants; recipient cofunds at least 50% of costs
grants.deadline_note: Rolling consideration; Murdock uses an inquiry-then-proposal process. Confirm current process on Murdock's site.
grants.fit: Medium-High – PNW-focused funder of 501(c)(3) capacity building; values diversified funding and community flourishing.
grants.eligibility: 501(c)(3) nonprofits and tribal entities in the Pacific Northwest. Requires recipient to cover at least 50% of project costs.
grants.use: Capacity-building projects, essential equipment/technology, new programs or program expansion.
grants.summary: Murdock is a major Pacific Northwest funder supporting capacity building, program expansion, and equipment/technology for 501(c)(3)s. It values organizations with diversified funding and clear community impact. Expect a cost-share requirement (recipient covers ~50%) and an inquiry-first process. A good fit for funding internal systems, staff capacity, or technology that supports Proud Ground's growth.

grants.name: Tenant & Housing Justice Grant
grants.funder: Social Justice Fund Northwest
grants.deadline_note: Annual cycle. Confirm 2026/2027 open window on SJF NW's site.
grants.fit: Medium – centers tenant/housing-justice organizing; relevance depends on Proud Ground's advocacy/organizing activities.
grants.eligibility: Grassroots organizations in ID, MT, OR, WA, and/or WY using a community-organizing framework; prioritizes communities underrepresented in traditional grantmaking.
grants.use: Community organizing to create alternatives to exploitative housing systems—e.g., tenants' rights, eviction prevention, housing-justice power building.
grants.summary: SJF Northwest funds grassroots housing-justice organizing across five PNW states, prioritizing communities underrepresented in traditional grantmaking. The strongest fit is for any tenant-rights, eviction-prevention, or community power-building organizing Proud Ground does alongside its homeownership work. Frame around organizing and systemic change rather than direct service.

grants.name: Community Grants & Sponsorships
grants.funder: OnPoint Community Credit Union
grants.deadline_note: Rolling/periodic. Confirm current open application on OnPoint's community giving page.
grants.fit: Medium – local PNW credit union funding economic opportunity and community development, including financial education and community development.
grants.eligibility: Nonprofits aligned with Economic Opportunity and Community Vitality focus areas (PNW).
grants.use: Financial education, workforce development, community development initiatives.
needed: Alignment with Economic Opportunity / Community Vitality
grants.summary: OnPoint is a Portland-based credit union that funds economic opportunity and community vitality, including financial education and community development. Proud Ground's homebuyer education and financial-readiness programming aligns well. A good local relationship-building funder; confirm the current application window on their community giving page.

grants.name: Competitive Affordable Housing Program (AHP)
grants.funder: Federal Home Loan Bank of Des Moines
grants.amount: Up to $3,000,000 per project ($150,000 max subsidy per unit)
grants.deadline_note: 2026 round closed May 1, 2026 (awards announced Dec 2026). 2027 round expected to open ~April 1, 2027. Requires partnership with an FHLB member bank.
grants.fit: Very High – one of the nation's largest sources of affordable housing project grants; covers purchase, construction, and rehab of homeownership units.
grants.eligibility: Nonprofit sponsors must partner with an FHLB Des Moines member financial institution to apply.
grants.use: Purchase, construction, or rehabilitation of affordable homeownership or rental housing units.
needed: FHLB Des Moines member bank partner (secure early)
grants.summary: The AHP is among the largest affordable-housing grant sources in the U.S. (over $1B awarded since 1990). Grants up to $3M per project support construction and rehab of homeownership units—directly aligned with Proud Ground's CLT development pipeline. The catch: you must partner with an FHLB member bank. Start identifying a member-bank partner now so you're ready when the 2027 window opens around April 1.

grants.name: Housing Affordability Breakthrough Challenge
grants.funder: Wells Fargo / Enterprise Community Partners
grants.deadline_note: 2026 cycle ran April 1 – May 15, 2026 (closed). Next cycle expected ~spring 2027. Three-round competition.
grants.fit: Medium-High – rewards scalable, innovative housing solutions; the CLT shared-equity model could qualify under Finance or Service & Delivery.
grants.eligibility: Nonprofit and for-profit orgs with demonstrated early results and a strategy to scale. Priority scoring for organizations in select states.
grants.use: Scaling an innovative housing solution in Design & Construction, Finance, or Service & Delivery.
grants.summary: A high-dollar national competition ($2M per winner) for proven, scalable housing innovations. Proud Ground's permanently-affordable shared-equity CLT model is a strong narrative fit under the Finance or Service & Delivery categories. It's competitive and multi-round, so best pursued with a clearly differentiated, data-backed innovation. Watch for the spring 2027 opening.

grants.name: Neighborhood Builders®
grants.funder: Bank of America Charitable Foundation
grants.amount: $100,000 – $400,000 over two years (capped at 10% of annual revenue)
grants.deadline_note: 2026 application window was June 1 – July 1, 2026. Recurs annually around the same window. Confirm your local market is selected.
grants.fit: High – explicitly funds creation/preservation of affordable housing and homeownership opportunities, plus leadership development.
grants.eligibility: 501(c)(3) nonprofits in selected markets. Cannot have received Neighborhood Builders/Champions funding since Oct 2019. Grant capped at 10% of most recent annual revenue.
grants.use: Capacity building + flexible grant; leadership development for ED and an emerging leader. 2026 funding areas include stable housing/homeownership.
needed: Confirm Portland/your market is selected for the cycle
ED + emerging leader for leadership program
grants.summary: Neighborhood Builders pairs a sizeable flexible grant ($100K–$400K over two years) with a two-year leadership development program for your ED and an emerging leader. Stable housing and homeownership are named 2026 funding areas. Note the grant can't exceed 10% of annual revenue, and your market must be selected in a given cycle. A strong recurring target—plan for the ~June 2027 window.
